div.l: Eke plato he seith whoso can̄ him rede
The wurdis mut be cosyn to the ovne dede
Also I pray you to foryeue it me
Al haue I not sette folk in her degre
Here in this tale as þat þey shuld stond
My witte is short ye may wel vndirstond .
¶ Greet chere made oure host us euerichone
And to the Souper sette he us anone
He ʆserued us with vitaile at the best
Strong was the wine ⁊and wel to drink us lest
A semely man oure host was withall
Forto be a marchal in any halle
A large man he was with eyen stepe
A feirer bourgeis was ther none in chepe
Bold of his speche and wise and wel y taught̄
And of manhode him lackid right nought
Eke therto he was right a mery man̄
And aftir Souper to pley he began̄
And spac of myrth among othir thingis .
Whan that we had made oure rekenyngꝭes
And seid thus / now lordis truly
Ye ben to me welcum right hertily
For be my trouth if I shal not lye
I saugh not this yere so mery a cūmpany
Attones / in this herborou as be now .
Fayn̄ wold I do you mirth wist I how .
And of a mirth now right I am bethought̄
To do you ease and it shal cost you nought̄
Ye gone to Cauntirbury god you spede
The blisful martir quite you your mede
And wel I wote as ye gone by the wey
Ye shapen you tales and to pley
For truly cumfort ne mirth is ther none
To ride by the wey dombe as eny stone
And therfore wil I make you disport
As I seid erst / and do you sum̄ cumfort
And if you liked alle by one assent
Forto stond hole atte my Iugement
And forto werken as I shalle you sey
To morou whan ye riden̄ by the wey
